title: The Sampo: A Threefold Mill
subtitle: Ilmarinen's forge produces an extraordinary object

mill.author: Elias Lönnrot, compiler and editor
mill.locator: Rune X · Ilmarinen forges the Sampo; Rune X · Ilmarinen forges the Sampo, normalized characters 14386-14715
mill.excerpt: On one side the flour is grinding, On another salt is making, On a third is money forging, And the lid is many-colored. Well the Sampo grinds when finished, To and fro the lid in rocking, Grinds one measure at the day-break, Grinds a measure fit for eating, Grinds a second for the market, Grinds a third one for the store-house.
mill.note: Verbatim English verse translated by John Martin Crawford from Lönnrot's nineteenth-century compilation of oral poetry; not a transcript of one ancient or single oral witness.

narrativeBlocks.title: The bride-price of Pohjola
narrativeBlocks.body: To win the maiden of the North, the smith Ilmarinen is set the impossible task: forge the Sampo — a magic mill no one has ever made.

narrativeBlocks.title: A thing hammered from scraps
narrativeBlocks.body: The forging is the poem's great passage: from swan-feather tips, the milk of barren kine, a grain of barley — scraps of the world made into something magic by skill.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mill that grinds fortune
narrativeBlocks.body: The Sampo is finished: a threefold mill that grinds out flour, salt, and money — food, trade, and wealth — prosperity itself, produced on demand.

narrativeBlocks.title: A prize that brings war
narrativeBlocks.body: Louhi of the North claims the prize — and the Sampo becomes the Kalevala's great prize-object: its pursuit and loss drive the whole second half of the epic.

narrativeBlocks.title: Finland's Philosopher's Stone
narrativeBlocks.body: The Sampo is the Kalevala's signature marvel — the prosperity-machine that the whole epic's heroes scheme, fight, and mourn over.
